title: States of Matter
description: Matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas. Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow and take the shape of their container. Gases spread out to fill their space.

exercises.question: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?
exercises.exp: Solids keep their shape. A rock is always rock-shaped!

exercises.question: Water is a LIQUID. What does a liquid do?
choices: takes the shape of its container
exercises.exp: Liquids flow and take the shape of whatever holds them — like juice in a glass!

exercises.question: Which of these is a GAS?
exercises.exp: Air is a gas — it spreads everywhere and you cannot see it.

exercises.question: A SOLID apple is cut into pieces. Is it still a solid?
choices: yes, each piece is still a solid
exercises.exp: Cutting a solid does not change its state. Each apple piece is still a solid!

exercises.question: Which of these is a LIQUID?
exercises.exp: Orange juice is a liquid — it flows and takes the shape of its cup.

exercises.question: Where can a GAS go?
choices: it spreads to fill any space
exercises.exp: Gases spread out to fill whatever space they are in, like air in a room.

exercises.question: Sort these into the correct state: steam, ice, water
exercises.exp: Steam = gas, ice = solid, water = liquid. Three states of the same substance!

exercises.question: Which has a DEFINITE (fixed) volume?
exercises.exp: Solids have a fixed shape AND volume. Gases expand to fill their container.

exercises.question: A balloon is filled with air. The air is a ___.
exercises.exp: Air is a gas. It fills the balloon and keeps it puffed up.

exercises.question: Which is NOT a liquid?
exercises.exp: Sand is made of tiny solid grains — it is a solid, not a liquid.

exercises.question: Ice cream left on a warm day becomes ___.
exercises.exp: Heat melts ice cream from solid to liquid — it drips!

exercises.question: Which state of matter can you NOT hold in your hand?
exercises.exp: Gas (air) spreads out — you cannot hold it in your hand like a solid or liquid.

exercises.question: Which property do ALL solids share?
choices: they have a fixed shape and volume
exercises.exp: All solids have a definite shape and volume — they do not change shape unless you cut or break them.

exercises.question: You pour juice from a tall glass into a wide bowl. The juice takes the shape of the bowl. This shows juice is a ___.
exercises.exp: Liquids always take the shape of their container — juice in a bowl spreads out flat, in a glass it is tall and narrow.

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT a solid?
exercises.exp: Steam is a gas — it spreads out into the air. Coins, bricks, and crayons are all solids.

exercises.question: When you blow up a balloon, the air inside is a ___.
exercises.exp: Air is a gas — it fills the entire balloon and pushes outward on the walls.

exercises.question: Which is an example of a GAS?
exercises.exp: Steam is a gas (water vapour) — it rises and spreads into the air from boiling water.

exercises.question: Honey is a thick liquid. Is it still a liquid?
choices: no, it is a solid because it is thick
yes, it flows and takes the shape of its container
it is a mixture of solid and liquid
exercises.exp: Honey is definitely a liquid — it flows (slowly!) and takes the shape of any jar or bottle.

exercises.question: Oxygen gas in a tank is COMPRESSED (squeezed). It is still a ___.
exercises.exp: Compressing a gas squeezes the particles closer together, but it is still a gas — just denser.

exercises.question: Which would happen if you put a solid square block into a round container?
choices: it would change into a round shape
it would stay square and not fill the round container
exercises.exp: Solids keep their own shape — the square block stays square even in a round container.

exercises.question: What is the difference between a liquid and a gas?
choices: liquids are always cold; gases are always hot
liquids have a fixed volume; gases spread to fill their container
exercises.exp: A liquid has a fixed volume but no fixed shape. A gas has no fixed shape OR volume — it fills any container!

exercises.question: Jelly (gelatin) is wobbly but keeps its shape. It is a ___.
exercises.exp: Jelly is a solid — it holds its own shape even though it is soft and wobbly!

exercises.question: What is another word for a gas changing into a liquid?
exercises.exp: Condensing (condensation) is when a gas cools and turns into a liquid — like steam becoming water drops.

exercises.question: Which state of matter has particles that are FARTHEST apart?
exercises.exp: Gas particles are spread very far apart with lots of empty space between them.

exercises.question: Which of these is a SOLID at room temperature?
exercises.exp: A wooden chair is a solid — it keeps its shape at room temperature.

exercises.question: You open a bottle of perfume. The smell spreads across the room. This happens because ___.
choices: the perfume is a solid spreading
the perfume evaporates and gas particles spread through the air
the room is full of water
exercises.exp: Perfume particles become a gas and diffuse (spread) through the air — that is how you smell it far away!

exercises.question: Which characteristic is TRUE for both liquids AND gases?
choices: they flow and can change shape
exercises.exp: Both liquids and gases flow — they do not have a fixed shape. But only gases lack a fixed volume too.

exercises.question: Sand poured into a container takes the shape of the container. Does this make it a liquid?
choices: yes, it flows like a liquid
no, each grain of sand is a solid — sand is a collection of tiny solids
yes, it is a special type of liquid
exercises.exp: Sand looks like it flows, but each tiny grain is a solid with its own fixed shape — sand is a granular solid!

exercises.question: You squeeze a balloon — it squishes. You cannot squish a rock. This shows that ___.
choices: gases can be compressed but solids are almost incompressible
solids and gases behave the same
liquids are easier to compress than gases
exercises.exp: Gas particles have lots of space between them so they can be squeezed. Solid particles are already packed tight!

exercises.question: Which of these would fill a large container AND a small container completely?
exercises.exp: A gas expands to fill any container completely — from a tiny bottle to a large room!

exercises.question: Water at room temperature is a liquid. The SAME water in a freezer becomes ___.
exercises.exp: In the freezer, water cools to 0°C and freezes into solid ice — same H₂O, different state!

exercises.question: Which state of matter has a DEFINITE shape and a DEFINITE volume?
exercises.exp: Solids keep their own shape and take up the same amount of space no matter which container you put them in.

exercises.question: Milk is poured into a round cup and then a square cup. The milk ___.
choices: stays the same shape both times
takes the shape of each cup but keeps the same volume
exercises.exp: Liquids have a fixed volume but take the shape of any container they are poured into!

exercises.question: What are the THREE common states of matter?
exercises.exp: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid, and gas. (Plasma is a fourth state but rare on Earth.)

exercises.question: Which property is shared by ALL matter?
choices: it takes up space and has mass
exercises.exp: All matter takes up space (has volume) and has mass — whether it is a rock, water, or the air around you!

exercises.question: Air is a ___.
exercises.exp: Air is a gas — it has no fixed shape or volume, and its particles spread out to fill any space.

exercises.question: A solid keeps its shape because ___.
choices: its particles are not moving at all
its particles are tightly packed and vibrate in fixed positions
there is no space between particles
exercises.exp: In a solid, particles vibrate but stay locked in place — this tight packing gives a solid its fixed shape.

exercises.question: When you pour juice into a glass, the juice takes the shape of the glass. Juice is a ___.
exercises.exp: Juice is a liquid — it flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping the same volume.

exercises.question: Which observation would tell you a sample of matter is a GAS?
choices: it stays in a pile on the table
it spreads out and fills the whole room
exercises.exp: Gases spread out to fill all available space. If your sample spreads everywhere, it is definitely a gas!

exercises.question: In which state are particles CLOSEST together?
exercises.exp: Solid particles are packed most tightly together — that is why solids are usually the most dense state.

exercises.question: Why can you pour water but not pour a rock?
choices: water is a liquid — its particles slide past each other; rock is solid with fixed particles
exercises.exp: Liquid particles slide past each other freely, allowing flow. Solid particles are locked in place and cannot flow.

exercises.question: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide. When it gets warmer it turns directly into gas — no liquid! This is called ___.
exercises.exp: Sublimation is when a solid changes directly to a gas without passing through the liquid stage. Dry ice does this!

exercises.question: Which of these is a GAS at room temperature?
exercises.exp: Oxygen is a gas at room temperature — it is all around us in the air we breathe!

exercises.question: The particles in a liquid move ___.
choices: slowly past each other, staying close but not locked in place
exercises.exp: Liquid particles slide past each other — slower than gas particles, but freer than solid particles.

exercises.question: If you remove the lid from a jar of hot cocoa, the steam you see is water ___.
choices: condensing back into tiny droplets visible in the air
exercises.exp: The 'steam' you see is water vapour that has cooled slightly and condensed into tiny visible water droplets.

exercises.question: A gas ALWAYS has a fixed volume. True or False?
choices: False — gas expands or contracts to fill any container
exercises.exp: False! Gases expand to fill any container. That is why a balloon expands when you blow air into it.

exercises.question: You put a chocolate bar in a hot car. It melts into liquid. The chocolate's mass has ___.
exercises.exp: Melting is a physical change — only the state changes, not the amount. The mass of the chocolate stays the same!

exercises.question: Which type of matter has particles that are very far apart and move very fast?
exercises.exp: Gas particles move fast and are spread far apart with lots of empty space between them.

exercises.question: Is toothpaste a solid or a liquid?
choices: it behaves like both — it holds shape but flows when pushed
exercises.exp: Toothpaste is a non-Newtonian fluid — it behaves like a solid at rest but flows like a liquid when you squeeze it!

exercises.question: What happens to the VOLUME of a gas when you pump it into a smaller container?
choices: it gets compressed into the smaller space
it turns into a liquid instantly
exercises.exp: Gas can be compressed — squeezing it into a smaller space increases its pressure. Bicycle tyres use this!

exercises.question: In science, the word 'matter' means ___.
choices: anything that has mass and takes up space
exercises.exp: In science, matter is ANYTHING that has mass and takes up space — solids, liquids, gases, even things you cannot see!
